source.review_note: Root and independent chassis peer approved exact2022 source and153 ordered steps with retained-ECU adaptation, single shared pivot, deferred exhaust-access joints, exact lower-holder access and mandatory externally documented wheel-seal endpoints/oil-check closure. Physical validation remains separate.

title: Strip the stock frame, renew chassis bearings and reassemble the bike
completeness: Exact2022 assembled stock bike to exposed serviceable main frame, then steering, swingarm/linkage, wheel and sealed shock-eye bearing renewal and reassembly. Conditional on documented exact wheel-seal endpoints and oil-check-bolt closure acquired before work. Bonded pads remain; no structural repair or engine internal completion is implied.

applicability.included: Exact stock US2022YZ450F / YZ450FN with serviceable frame and original interfaces, documented required external closure values and intact working brake/chain holding system.
excluded: Internal engine repairs unless separately source-reviewed and recorded
Wheel/frame/suspension bearing service or structural repair
Complete cable replacement or throttle-body sensor/calibration work
Broken chain, failed rear brake or seized sprocket nut preventing the reviewed manual holding method
ECU mounting-fastener service: source table3.8Nm conflicts with exploded8Nm; retained mounts are not disturbed.
Oil-level check-bolt torque/seal prescription: documented exact-interface closure required before work.
Structural frame repair, pressed-seat machining, paint stripping and removal of bonded pads.
Unknown wheel-seal seating endpoints: obtain exact-interface documentation before this route.
Tire/spoke/sprocket replacement and internal suspension service are separate.

prerequisites: Before beginning, obtain and record a documented exact2022 oil-level check-bolt refit torque/seal requirement from an attributed source or qualified Yamaha service provider. The manual requires opening it for final level but does not defensibly identify its closure torque; no generic cover or pressure-check bolt value is adopted.
Confirm exact stock engine, intact chain and working rear brake. Photograph all routing, shim positions and control settings.

Independent chassis, engine, swingarm and shock support is required. Lower shock and frame-side connecting-arm bolts are released for exhaust clearance; remaining linkage joints are removed once in the frame stage.

ECU and ignition coil stay mounted on the aircase. Confirm the complete retained assembly can be lifted after disconnecting its identified couplers and plug cap without blocking the three case bolts or loading wiring. If actual clearance requires ECU removal, resolve its conflicting source torque first.
Any separate internal bench work must return sealed covers/filter/strainer and documented timing, clearances, lubrication and free rotation. No internals are serviced here.
A replaced cylinder-head gasket needs the separate OEM266 warm3-minute pressure-test method; the retained-gasket cold check here does not complete that requirement.
Document exact front/rear hub seal seating endpoints and source before dismantling. OEM2022 does not specify the later0mm/1mm numeric depths; unknown endpoints are not inferred.
Confirm all universal bearing-tool drivers/receivers physically fit the actual interface, load only the fitted ring and support the housing without obscuring required depth measurements.
Bonded pads remain; serviceable frame geometry is required. Steering races and removable controls/closed hydraulics are removed, while ECU and coil remain mounted to aircase.

required_tools.name: Stable motorcycle stand plus independent engine, swingarm and shock supports, temporary pivot-support shaft and helper
Calibrated torque tools covering 1.5-135 Nm; correct sockets and manual breaker bar
Fuel-safe transfer equipment, containers, measured oil/coolant vessels and port covers

Configured Yamaha diagnostic tool 90890-03269 (US USB) or 90890-03264, FI sub-lead90890-03212/YU-03212 and OBD/GST lead kit90890-03249 with supplied instructions; digital tachometer 90890-06760/YU-39951-B
Ruler/free-play gauge, means of applying approximately 50 N for chain slack; source-specific molybdenum-disulfide and lithium-soap greases
Calibrated torque tools additionally reaching145Nm, accurate at5/7/12/28/42/55/56/70/80Nm for chassis joints
Steering nut wrench90890-01403/YU-A9472 used at right angle; cap ring wrench90890-01501/YM-01501
Motion Pro08-0544 stem tool and08-0669 race installer with actual fitting drivers/adapter;14/24mm wrenches and protective block/soft mallet
Motion Pro08-0294 bearing tool with actual fitting needle-support mandrels and receivers; appropriate vise support
Hub bearing pullers, matching outer-race/seal drivers, circlip pliers and protective cloth/screwdriver
Depth gauge and straight references for exact source dimensions and externally documented wheel-seal endpoints
Stable dial gauge mount for rim radial/lateral runout on installed supported axles
Long rod/hammer and chisel for OEM race removal; clean storage and kerosene for specified cleaning

required_parts.name: New coolant drain copper washer and specified coolant
New exact sprocket lock washer and stock-chain joint clip
New exhaust-port gasket and two pipe-joint gaskets
Recommended engine oil
required_parts.purpose: Recorded.63/.65/.90L case selection and exact level/flow verification.

required_parts.name: Molybdenum-disulfide grease and lithium-soap grease
required_parts.purpose: Pivot and released suspension bolts M; pedal O-rings/pivot and throttle contacts LS.

required_parts.name: Oil-level check-bolt sealing parts required by separately documented exact-interface closure
required_parts.purpose: Do not infer a seal or torque from another fastener.

required_parts.name: Exact new matched steering bearings/races/dust seal
Exact wheel bearings, seals and new rear circlip
required_parts.purpose: Front2 and rear3 bearings; four seal endpoints must be externally documented before work.

required_parts.name: New rear sprocket self-locking nuts
required_parts.purpose: Six removed during wheel work; original serviceable sprocket retained.

required_parts.name: Exact new swingarm bearings/bushes/seals and serviceable thrust bearings/collars
required_parts.purpose: Four bearings/four seals; source depth and stack checks.

required_parts.name: Exact new linkage bearings/collars/seals
required_parts.purpose: Six bearings/six seals; eight relay washers retained if serviceable.

required_parts.name: Exact new shock-eye bushings/bearing, seals, O-rings and stopper ring
required_parts.purpose: Closed shock eyes only; no gas release.

required_parts.name: OEM-specified LOCTITE locking agent
required_parts.purpose: Footrest-bracket and wheel-disc bolts only, not the dry2022 drive-sprocket nut; record actual product, grade unspecified.

critical_stop_conditions: Unstable support, bent/cracked parts, damaged fasteners or unknown assembly order.
Binding, leaks, missing hardware or abnormal brake/control function remains an unresolved fault.

steps.title: Record the engine and job condition
steps.instruction: Record the exact stock engine identity, running condition and reason for removal. Photograph hose, electrical and bracket routing before access. Prepare an independently supported engine bench and a controlled lift with a helper; this guide removes/installs the assembly and does not repair its internals. Record initial clutch lever free play 7-12 mm and control condition before removing any cable end. Record the exact oil-level check-bolt closure document, applicable fastener/seal and torque before proceeding; this value is not established by the available manual. Also acquire and record exact front/rear hub seal-seating endpoints from an attributed exact-interface source before removing any wheel seals. OEM2022 lacks the later numeric recess values; never infer0mm/1mm. Record stock frame, wheel and bearing identities, existing condition and complete routing photographs.
verification: Exact bike, bench/supports, routing, initial7-12mm clutch free play and external check-bolt closure document recorded.
Exact front/rear wheel seal endpoint documents and installed hub identities recorded before work.

steps.title: Record the original cable positions
steps.instruction: Record pull/return cable positions at the grip against the exact handlebar diagram and actual grip free play, specified3-6mm. Preserve routing and adjustment without swapping cables.
verification: Original cable positions and actual free play recorded.

steps.title: Drain the engine oil before lifting
steps.instruction: For a normally running engine, warm for several minutes, stop and wait about5minutes; do not run a faulted engine solely to warm oil. Stand upright on level ground. Remove filler cap and the single drain bolt over a container. Leave filter/strainer assembled unless separately serviced. Drain completely and refit the drain with a new gasket at20Nm. Mark the engine empty.
verification: One drain closed with new gasket20Nm; engine marked empty.

steps.title: Prepare the bike
steps.instruction: Stop the engine, let it cool and support the bike. Clean the intake and fuel work area. Keep dirt out of open joints and fuel work away from ignition sources.
verification: Cold engine; stable bike; clean work area; parts/tools ready.

steps.title: Open the sub-seat
steps.instruction: Lift the fuel-tank-cap cover with fingers under both sides, upward toward the rear as illustrated; retain its plastic-band attachment to the seat. Open cap, transfer fuel to an appropriate container with fuel-safe equipment, then secure cap.
verification: Cap cover released intact; fuel safely contained and cap secured.

steps.title: Remove access panels
steps.instruction: Remove the left side-cover fasteners first, then the seat fasteners and slide the seat rearward with its attached cap cover. Remove the right side cover by releasing its illustrated projections from the slots. Label collars and fastener positions.
verification: Both covers and seat removed without damaging projections or plastic band.

steps.title: Isolate the battery
steps.instruction: With the engine stopped, disconnect the negative battery lead first, then the positive lead. Insulate the loose terminals. Retain the battery and relay in place unless separate frame work requires removal; no starter action is allowed during the work.
verification: Negative then positive disconnected and insulated.

steps.title: Expose the tank
steps.instruction: Loosen the air-filter-cover quick-fastener screw. Release its two ribs from the air-scoop projections and slide the cover forward. Keep the filter installed. Remove left/right air scoops, releasing their illustrated projections, grooves and slots without prying. Retain collars.
verification: Forward cover removal and scoop locators preserved; filter remains sealed.

steps.title: Disconnect the tank
steps.instruction: Unplug the fuel-pump connector. Put cloths below and around the fuel-hose joint for residual pressure. Remove the connector holder, slide the cover back, press its two release buttons and separate the joint by hand. Fit the supplied joint covers to both openings immediately.
verification: Pump disconnected; both fuel openings capped; no forced hose tools.

steps.title: Lift the tank clear
steps.instruction: Remove the tank mounting fasteners, retaining the collars/dampers in their original locations, and lift the tank away. Support it so its weight does not rest on the fuel-pump mounting surface. Leave the pump installed in the tank.
verification: Tank supported; mounts accounted for; pump untouched.

steps.title: Release the intact case
steps.instruction: Label and unplug ECU and ignition-coil couplers, disconnect intake-temperature coupler and pull the plug cap clear without removing the spark plug. Leave ECU and coil bolted to the aircase. Release only the routing clips needed to free their leads. Loosen case joint clamp and remove its three mounting bolts with original collars/washers/dampers. Do not disturb the ECU bolts because the manual gives conflicting tightening values.
verification: Retained ECU/coil assembly disconnected from harness and plug; case bolts/clamp accessible without disturbing ECU mounts.

steps.title: Lift off and protect the intake
steps.instruction: Lift the complete aircase with retained ECU, coil and filter off the intake joint, supporting its high-tension lead and plug cap. Stop if a mount is inaccessible or the retained assembly cannot clear freely; do not force it or remove ECU mounts without resolving their torque conflict. Cover exposed intake and keep the removed assembly clean.
verification: Case/ECU/coil clear and supported; inlet protected; all retained mounts unchanged.

steps.title: Open the cable housing
steps.instruction: Pull back the rubber cover. Remove the housing screws and separate the throttle cable housing without pulling on the cables.
verification: Housing open; rubber cover and screws retained.

steps.title: Release the two grip-end cables
steps.instruction: Disengage the pull and return cable ends from their original seats in the throttle tube as shown. Support the cables without kinking them and withdraw the complete grip/tube assembly from the bar. Do not peel the bonded rubber grip off its tube or disturb the cable ends at the throttle body.
verification: Both identified ends released; intact grip/tube retained.

steps.title: Check the released parts
steps.instruction: Inspect the tube sliding surface and cable-end seats for damage and check that the cables move without binding. Keep dirt out of the open housing. A damaged or frayed cable needs a separate full cable-renewal operation before this access job can return to service.
verification: Retained parts accepted; no damaged cable or binding.

steps.title: Support suspension and open the exhaust clearance path
steps.instruction: Support chassis, swingarm/rear wheel and shock independently so neither released joint carries spring or bike load. Remove the shock lower bolt and connecting-arm frame-side bolt as the exhaust prerequisites require. Preserve collars/seals and support the arm/shock without hanging from the remaining joints. Keep upper shock and other linkage pivots assembled.
verification: Two required access bolts removed under support; collars/seals retained; other joints untouched.

steps.title: Remove the complete silencer
steps.instruction: Support the silencer. Loosen its joint clamp, remove its two mounting bolts and lift the complete silencer off its joint. Keep the silencer body, end cap and packing assembled.
verification: Complete silencer supported and removed; internals untouched.

steps.title: Remove the intermediate pipe
steps.instruction: Loosen pipe2 joint clamp and remove its bracket bolt while supporting the pipe. With the shock lower and frame-side connecting-arm joints already released, move pipe2 through the exact illustrated clearance path and remove without forcing adjacent parts.
verification: Exhaust2 clear without load on unsupported suspension or hoses.

steps.title: Remove the header and old seals
steps.instruction: Remove the header nuts and header pipe. Leave the header protector attached. Remove the old exhaust-port gasket at the cylinder head and the two pipe-joint gaskets; inspect joint faces and supports for damage before refitting.
verification: Header removed; all three separated joint seals identified; protector untouched.

steps.title: Set up for a cold drain
steps.instruction: Stand the cooled bike upright on a level surface. Place the collection container beneath the engine and position it close to the drain outlet, because flow can shoot sideways when the radiator cap is released.
verification: Bike stable; engine and coolant cold; collection ready.

steps.title: Open the drain and radiator cap
steps.instruction: Remove the coolant drain bolt and its copper washer. Place a thick cloth over the radiator cap and turn it slowly counterclockwise toward its detent to release residual pressure. Once hissing stops, press down and turn farther to remove the cap. Let the coolant drain into the container. Thoroughly flush the cooling system with clean tap water as Yamaha directs, then drain the flush water completely before fitting the new drain washer. Account for residual water when establishing the final coolant mixture.
verification: Drain complete; old washer removed; cap opened only when cold.

steps.title: Install a new drain washer
steps.instruction: Install a new copper washer and the coolant drain bolt. Tighten the bolt to 10 N·m.
verification: New washer installed; drain bolt 10 N·m.

steps.title: Disconnect the engine coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Identify radiator hoses 1,3 and 4 from the source drawing. Mark each hose and clamp position, loosen its engine-side clamp and release the hoses from the engine. Keep radiators mounted and protect the open hose/engine ports from dirt. Do not remove coolant pipe joints or the temperature sensor itself.
verification: Hoses 1/3/4 labeled and clear; pipe joints/sensor remain sealed.

steps.title: Lift the intact throttle body from the engine joint
steps.instruction: Label/disconnect injector, intake-pressure and throttle-position sensor couplers. Keep sensors installed. Clean lower joint, loosen clamp and lift intact throttle body clear. Support its detached grip-end cables without tension; body-end seats, screws and pulley stay untouched. Cover engine inlet and body openings; never push the throttle valve.
verification: Three identified sensor/injector couplers disconnected; complete body/cables separately supported; calibration untouched.

steps.title: Disconnect the left engine harness interfaces
steps.instruction: Release only the retaining clips/ties needed to free engine leads. Disconnect the stator, crankshaft-position and gear-position connectors; keep the gear-position switch bolted to the engine so its seal is not disturbed. Match connector identity to the diagrams, using the actual labeled connectors and exact source routing. Label and protect both halves.
verification: Stator/crank-position/gear-position leads released; sensor seals untouched.

steps.title: Disconnect starter, ground and plug interfaces
steps.instruction: Disconnect coolant-temperature coupler and remove the head ground terminal bolt. Plug cap was released with the retained aircase group. At the starter lead pull back its rubber terminal cover and hold the motor-side nut with a spanner while undoing the lead nut. Release necessary lead clips and support harness clear. Leave motor and rigid motor covers installed; if terminal access is blocked, do not force it.
verification: Ground, temperature and starter lead free; isolated battery; motor/covers retained.

steps.title: Remove chain, sprocket and shift pedal
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel still secured, chain intact and rear brake still fully mounted, select neutral. Remove the sprocket cover and retained drive-chain guide, label their arrangement, and flatten the old lock-washer tabs. Have a helper hold the rear brake firmly while using a correctly fitting socket and manual breaker bar to loosen the sprocket nut, following the attributed Nick Dole technique. Do not use impact, heat or jam the chain against the case. Once loose, release the stock chain joint and remove the chain, retaining its matched link/plate and preparing a new clip. Remove the nut, old lock washer and sprocket. Mark and remove the shift pedal, preserving punch-mark alignment.
verification: Chain and sprocket clear; old lock washer/clip retired; shift position recorded.

source_links.title: Nick Dole manual rear-brake holding technique

steps.title: Disconnect and record the cable clutch
steps.instruction: Record clutch lever free play and the cable-end/adjuster positions. Release cable tension with the handlebar adjuster as necessary. Disconnect the engine-end cable nipple from the push lever and release the cable outer from its bracket as shown in the inset; keep the push lever, shaft and clutch cover installed. Retain the cable with its handlebar lever and support it clear of the engine lifting path. This bike has a cable clutch.
verification: Engine-end nipple and outer detached and identified; push lever and clutch internals remain installed; cable supported.

steps.title: Clear pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Remove the engine guard, brake-pedal pivot bolt and return spring. Support the pedal with its master-cylinder linkage attached. Label and release the cylinder-head breather hose from the engine and its routing holders. Keep brake hydraulics closed.
verification: Guard/pedal/spring retained; breather clear; brake system closed.

steps.title: Support engine and swingarm before undoing mounts
steps.instruction: Support the engine independently. Support the swingarm and prepare a same-diameter temporary support shaft from its other side if needed when the pivot is withdrawn. Confirm every electrical connector, hose, intake assembly and cable is clear before loosening the engine mounts.
verification: Independent supports ready; all engine interfaces clear.

steps.title: Release the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Remove both upper brackets and the two lower brackets with four identified shims and their mapped hardware. Preserve left/right shim positions. Withdraw the pivot while maintaining swingarm support with the temporary shaft. Keep the engine independently supported until every mount is free.
verification: Two lower brackets/four shims identified; shared pivot removed once with swingarm supported.

steps.title: Lift the engine out to the right
steps.instruction: Lift the engine and move its lower part toward the right side of the chassis as shown in the OEM drawing, then transfer it to the prepared support. Stop if any interface catches. Keep the inlet, exhaust and fluid ports protected from contamination.
verification: Assembly removed to right; no trapped interface; engine stable.

steps.title: Support the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Keep the chassis independently supported with its rear wheel clear. The engine and drive chain are already removed. Protect the rear brake pedal against operation while the wheel is absent; keep the hydraulic line closed.
verification: Rear wheel clear, bike stable, brake pedal protected.

steps.title: Release the axle and chain
steps.instruction: Remove the rear axle nut. Loosen both adjuster locknuts and turn the adjusting bolts inward. Support the wheel, withdraw the axle and retain both pullers and collars by side. The chain was already removed for engine access; lower the wheel clear without disturbing the hydraulic line.
verification: Wheel clear; left/right pullers and collars labeled.

steps.title: Inspect wheel, axle and collars
steps.instruction: Check the axle for bending, the tire/wheel and collars for damage, and bearings for roughness or looseness. Inspect seals and sprocket teeth. Record defects; damaged components need the matching repair before refitting.
verification: Serviceability recorded; no damaged parts silently reused.

steps.title: Free the complete rear brake assembly
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel removed, slide the complete caliper/bracket off its swingarm guide and release the hose retaining clamps. The pedal pivot/spring were already removed during engine access. Remove the two rear-master-cylinder mounting bolts and support master, hose, caliper and linked pedal together. Keep hose unions, reservoir, pads and pushrod pin attached; do not pump the pedal.
verification: Entire rear brake assembly supported off frame/swingarm; hydraulic circuit remains closed.

steps.title: Unlink the shock and linkage
steps.instruction: Lower shock and connecting-arm frame bolts were already removed for exhaust access. Keep swingarm and shock supported. Remove ONLY connecting-arm-to-relay and relay-to-swingarm bolts now; keep each collar/washer/seal stack with its identified joint. Other removed bolts remain labeled for final closure.
verification: Previously released lower/frame joints not repeated; remaining two linkage joints identified and removed.

steps.title: Remove the supported swingarm
steps.instruction: The engine pivot is already withdrawn. Support the arm while removing the temporary support shaft used for engine removal, then lower the swingarm clear. Keep original collars and thrust-bearing/seal stacks with their correct sides. The linkage is already free; bearing/seal renewal follows the bare-frame inspection.
verification: Temporary pivot removed; supported arm clear; all stacks labeled.

steps.title: Inspect the arm, pivot and linkage
steps.instruction: Inspect swingarm and linkage arms for cracks, bending and damaged bearing bores. Roll the pivot on a flat surface to check straightness; never straighten a bent pivot. Record condition of bushes, collars, thrust bearings and washers. Replace damaged structural parts before installing new bearings. Bearing/bushing and linkage bearing/collar pairs are renewed as sets.
verification: Serviceability recorded for pivot, arm and every linkage joint.

steps.title: Remove the sealed shock
steps.instruction: Support the shock, remove its upper nut/bolt and lift out the complete sealed assembly. Its lower bolt was removed with the linkage. Keep the eyelet stacks identified until their bench renewal; do not release gas or loosen the preload hardware.
verification: Sealed shock and upper hardware supported and retained.

steps.title: Record and support
steps.instruction: Record both fork clicker settings and current height. This route restores exact2022 standard5mm projection. Independently support stripped chassis with front wheel clear; engine/rear wheel are removed.
verification: Actual settings recorded; exact5mm refit target and stand support established.

steps.title: Free the hose guides
steps.instruction: Remove plate bolt, release its band projection, and remove clutch cable from the plate guide. Pull plate off the lower steering-bracket projection. Keep the front brake hose in front of the plate without stress; do not copy a front-fender locating projection from another year.
verification: Plate/lower-bracket projection and clutch guide released; brake hose supported.

steps.title: Support the intact handlebar assembly
steps.instruction: Record both lower-holder offset orientations and the four rubber damper/washer positions against the source. Remove the two lower-holder nuts and lift the complete bar with upper/lower holders and controls still assembled. Retain all four dampers and washers in order. Support bar/closed hydraulics without loading cables; the throttle tube and grip-end cables are already detached. Leave the four upper-holder bolts untouched. With fork legs still clamped, loosen steering-stem nut for later removal.
verification: Lower-holder positions/four dampers recorded; complete bar/holders supported; upper-holder bolts unchanged.

steps.title: Remove the front wheel
steps.instruction: Loosen all four axle pinch bolts. Support the wheel; remove the axle nut and axle, then lower the wheel clear. Label and retain its left and right collars. Prevent the brake lever being operated with the disc absent.
verification: Wheel/axle/collars retained with correct sides; pads not forced closed.

steps.title: Support the brake assembly
steps.instruction: Remove the two caliper mounting bolts and support the complete caliper so its weight cannot pull on the hose. Keep the hose union, bleed screw, pad pin and pads undisturbed. Release the brake-hose holder from the fork protector, preserving its orientation and paint-mark position.
verification: Caliper supported; closed hydraulic circuit; hose not loaded.

steps.title: Remove the protectors
steps.instruction: Remove the three protector bolts on each fork leg and lift the protectors away. Keep the hardware grouped by side.
verification: Both protectors removed; hardware accounted for.

steps.title: Release each fork leg
steps.instruction: Support one fork leg. Loosen its upper-clamp pinch bolts, then use the specified ring wrench to loosen—but not remove—the damper assembly at the top while the lower clamp still holds the leg. Loosen the lower-clamp pinch bolts and slide the supported leg down and out. Repeat on the other side; keep assemblies upright and intact.
verification: Both legs supported and removed; caps only loosened; no oil drained or internal components removed.

steps.title: Check before refitting
steps.instruction: Keep the assemblies intact. Check for visible leakage, damage or abnormal movement. A fork that needs repair does not become serviced by completing this removal/refit task; route it to the separate repair operation.
verification: Assemblies suitable for refit or fault recorded; internal-service status not invented.

steps.title: Remove the front fender
steps.instruction: Remove its four bolts and retain the mounting hardware in order. Remove the steering-stem nut and lift away the upper bracket and its washer.
verification: Fender, upper bracket and washer retained; all supported.

steps.title: Lower the steering stem
steps.instruction: Support the lower bracket. Remove the ring nut using the steering-nut wrench, then lower the stem and retain the upper bearing and race cover. Photograph the lower seal and bearing stack and both head race orientations before disturbing them.
verification: Lower bracket supported and removed; bearing stack retained in order.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the steering bearings
steps.instruction: Clean and inspect the exposed steering seats, stem and upper/lower brackets. Record damage, pitting, cracks or bending. Replace structurally damaged parts before continuing; do not repair a damaged seat by forcing a new race into it.
verification: Retained brackets/stem and seats inspected; both old bearing/race sets are scheduled for renewal, not reuse.

steps.title: Remove the old matched bearing sets
steps.instruction: Use exact steering-head illustrations: remove both head races with long rod/hammer and lower-bracket race with chisel/hammer while protecting frame/stem. Discard old matched bearing/race sets. Clean/inspect empty seats before fitting new sets.
verification: Old matched sets removed; seats undamaged and clean.

steps.title: Remove the radiators and remaining hose connections
steps.instruction: Coolant was drained during engine access. Label all four hoses1–4 and every remaining clamp orientation using the source diagram. Release the remaining radiator-side hose joints and the radiator breather. Support each radiator, remove its two mounting bolts, and retain each damper/collar/washer stack. Lift both radiators and the loose hoses clear. Leave the coolant pipe joints and their O-rings on the removed engine.
verification: Both radiators/hoses labeled; four mount stacks retained; engine pipe seals untouched.

steps.title: Release the rear electrical attachments
steps.instruction: Battery already isolated. Release band and lift battery. Unplug CCU, main-relay and starter-relay harness couplers/covers; retain units/holders on rear frame. Free main loom clips/ties as shown. Keep starter/positive leads on relay and carry with rear-frame assembly; starter engine terminal is already free. ECU/coil were removed intact with aircase, not this rear frame.
verification: Rear couplers and clips free; retained rear units supported; ECU not falsely located on rear frame.

steps.title: Remove the rear-frame assembly
steps.instruction: Support the rear frame with rear fender and electronics holders attached. Remove its four mounting bolts and lift the assembly clear, checking no wire, silencer or hose remains attached. Keep bolts mapped by position. The upper chain roller is separately bolted on this 2022 frame; remove that bolt and retain the complete roller/collar stack separately.
verification: Four mapped bolts and separate upper roller/collar retained; no tethered group.

steps.title: Lift the supported controls and main harness clear
steps.instruction: Throttle body/cables and case/ECU/coil are already disconnected and supported separately. Release remaining frame holders/ties using exact routing. Unbolt rectifier/regulator but leave its housing intact. Identify/disconnect frame ground terminal and record its location. Lift main loom and supported bar/closed front brake/cable clutch clear without loading any line; do not remove nonexistent separate aircase/coil brackets from a later design. Keep switches and hydraulic circuits assembled.
verification: All groups independently supported; regulator/frame ground released; ECU/coil mounts retained.

steps.title: Remove the remaining bolt-on frame parts
steps.instruction: Remove each complete footrest bracket with its peg, spring and pin still assembled; retain the four bracket bolts by side. Remove the lower chain-tensioner bolt and intact roller/collar stack. Identify and retain any remaining clip-in harness holders and removable rubber mounting pieces in labeled positions. The steering races have been removed; bonded frame pads remain; this is not a paint-stripping or structural repair operation.
verification: Footrest assemblies and lower roller removed; remaining frame attachments recorded.

steps.title: Inspect the exposed main frame
steps.instruction: Clean and inspect the exposed main frame with both steering head races removed; retain bonded pads and identification markings. Record cracks, bends, thread/seat damage, corrosion or fretting. Structural repair, race-seat machining and alignment correction are outside this route. Confirm the frame is serviceable before installing races or continuing the following bench renewal stages.
verification: Frame condition and component repair status recorded; no structural fault silently accepted.

steps.title: Expose both sides of the hub
steps.instruction: Record the installed disc and sprocket faces/orientations before removal. Support the wheel without loading the disc. Remove the six sprocket self-locking nuts and retain the bolt/washer arrangement by location; remove the sprocket. Remove the six brake-disc bolts and lift off the disc. Keep friction surfaces clear of grease and locking agent.
verification: Sprocket/disc orientation and hardware recorded; hub accessible; disc protected.

steps.title: Remove seals and bearing retention
steps.instruction: Clean the hub exterior. Lever out both old oil seals with a flat-head screwdriver, using a cloth between tool and wheel to protect the hub. Remove the right-side bearing circlip with suitable circlip pliers before attempting to extract that bearing. Retain old seals and clip only for matching replacements.
verification: Both seals and right-side circlip removed; bearing retention released.

steps.title: Extract all three old bearings
steps.instruction: Use suitable bearing puller to remove single right bearing after circlip removal; retain internal spacer and remove both left bearings. Preserve side/order from exact exploded diagram. Support hub and do not pull against retained hardware.
verification: Three old bearings removed; right circlip already removed; spacer retained.

steps.title: Inspect the hub and spacer
steps.instruction: Clean and inspect bearing seats, circlip groove, internal spacer and external collars for damage or wear. Record whether the original hub and spacer remain serviceable. Check axle bending on a flat surface; do not straighten it. Check tire/wheel condition now; measure runout after the wheel is refitted on its axle as instructed in the final check. A damaged seat, spacer, axle, disc or worn sprocket requires its own repair/replacement decision; this guide does not authorize machining or truing.
verification: Hub/spacer/collars and axle condition recorded; no unresolved damage accepted; runout deferred until axle refit.

steps.title: Fit the right bearing first
steps.instruction: Install new right/disc-side bearing FIRST into original seat, pressing outer race square/parallel with matching driver. Seal faces outward as exact source instructs. Apply lithium-soap grease to bearing per source. Do not load inner race or spin with air.
verification: Right bearing first; outward sealed face; outer-race load only.

steps.title: Fit new right-side retention
steps.instruction: Install matching new right-side circlip with general edge/force orientation. Avoid overexpansion; verify full groove seating before seal. If groove is blocked, correct bearing/retainer fit rather than forcing clip.
verification: New correct circlip fully seated in right groove.

steps.title: Restore the spacer and both left bearings
steps.instruction: Locate original serviceable internal spacer between right bearing and left pair, then install both matching new left bearings in exact exploded order with outward sealed face. Grease bearings with lithium-soap grease and press outer races squarely with matching driver. Verify correct spacer location and smooth movement.
verification: Spacer retained; both left bearings installed with correct orientation and smooth stack.

steps.title: Install both new wheel seals
steps.instruction: Use the documented exact rear-hub seal-seating endpoint acquired before work; the available2022 manual does not give the later1mm numeric recess. Apply lithium-soap grease to new seal lips, marked faces outward and main lips toward hub. Drive each evenly with matching outer-diameter tool to that documented endpoint. Record both actual positions and source, then verify collar/seal engagement. Do not invent a recess from the drawing.
verification: Documented exact rear-hub endpoint and both actual seal positions recorded; no later-year1mm assumption.

steps.title: Refit the original serviceable sprocket
steps.instruction: Clean the hub/sprocket mating faces and restore the recorded original orientation and bolt/washer arrangement. This workflow uses matching new self-locking nuts. Tighten all six nuts progressively in a crisscross pattern to42 N·m. Inspect that the sprocket sits fully against the hub. Worn or bent teeth require matched drive/rear sprocket replacement outside this retained-sprocket operation.
verification: Six sprocket nuts42 N·m in staged crisscross pattern; mating faces seated.

steps.title: Refit the original serviceable disc
steps.instruction: Restore the recorded disc orientation against clean mating faces. Apply the specified LOCTITE locking agent at the disc-bolt threads and tighten all six bolts progressively in a crisscross pattern to12 N·m. The OEM source does not identify a grade or cure time here; record the actual product and follow its instructions. Keep grease/locking agent away from friction faces and inspect seating.
verification: Six disc bolts12 N·m in stages/crisscross; actual locking agent recorded; disc seated and friction faces clean.

steps.title: Inspect the removed wheel
steps.instruction: Roll the axle on a flat surface and replace it if bent; never straighten it. Inspect wheel, tire, disc and collars. Record bearing roughness or looseness and seal damage. Continue this bearing-renewal route only with a serviceable hub and no unresolved tire, rim, spoke or disc defect.
verification: Bearing/seal findings recorded; remaining wheel assembly is serviceable.

steps.title: Remove both oil seals
steps.instruction: Clean the outside of the hub. Use a flat-head screwdriver to lift out the oil seals, with a cloth between the screwdriver and hub to protect the wheel surface. Discard both removed seals.
verification: Both seals removed without damaging the hub.

steps.title: Pull both hub bearings
steps.instruction: Use a suitable bearing puller to remove both bearings. Retain the centre spacer and keep the left and right locations identified. Discard the removed bearings; do not load or bend the retained brake disc.
verification: Both bearings removed; centre spacer retained.

steps.title: Check the hub and spacer
steps.instruction: Confirm the bearing bores and spacer have not been damaged and are clean enough for the new bearings to seat correctly. A damaged or loose bearing fit needs separate wheel repair; do not conceal it with an improvised shim or adhesive.
verification: Record accepted hub/spacer condition or stop for wheel repair.

steps.title: Install the left bearing first
steps.instruction: Fit the new LEFT bearing first with its manufacturer marks or size symbols facing outward. Press it squarely by its outer race using a matching driver or socket, following the bearing position in the assembly diagram. Apply source-specified lithium-soap grease to bearing.
verification: Left bearing seated squarely; pressing load applied only to its outer race.

steps.title: Restore the spacer and right bearing
steps.instruction: Insert the centre spacer, then install the new RIGHT bearing with its manufacturer marks or size symbols facing outward. Press squarely on its outer race with the matching driver. Confirm the spacer remains correctly positioned between the bearings and the bearing seats as illustrated. Apply source-specified lithium-soap grease to bearing.
verification: Spacer present; right bearing squarely seated.

steps.title: Install both new oil seals
steps.instruction: Use documented exact front-hub seal-seating endpoint obtained before work; no later-year0mm depth is asserted by this2022 source. Grease lips with lithium-soap grease, marks outward/main lips toward hub, and install square with matching seal-diameter driver to that documented endpoint. Record actual position of both seals and source.
verification: Exact front-hub endpoint and actual seal positions recorded; no inferred flush setting.

steps.title: Check the renewed hub
steps.instruction: Turn the bearings and verify smooth movement without looseness. Confirm both seals and the centre spacer are correctly located before the side collars and axle are fitted. Resolve binding or a loose fit before returning the wheel to the bike.
verification: Record smooth bearings, no looseness and all internal parts present.

steps.title: Identify every bearing and seal stack
steps.instruction: Photograph both swingarm ends and each linkage joint against exact exploded diagrams. Remove collars,seals,thrust bearings,bushes and washers in order. Retain identified serviceable washers separately. Swingarm has four pivot bearings; relay four and connecting arm two, with eight relay washers. Do not mix washer groups or press through retained hardware.
verification: All original stacks recorded, four swingarm/six linkage bearings and eight relay washers accounted.

steps.title: Remove bearings with supported fitting tools
steps.instruction: Use Motion Pro08-0294 figures1-2/5 for accessible bearings: select a fitting driver, center the receiver and draw each bearing into the cup. Where opposite-side access is unavailable, figures7-8 show the fully engaged blind remover with greased puller threads/washer. First remove obstructions and check for hidden retainers. Stop if the receiver cannot support the housing squarely. Clean and inspect every empty bore.
verification: Tool fit/support and unobstructed removal path checked
Bores undamaged; no retained debris

source_links.title: Motion Pro tool technique; Yamaha depths control

steps.title: Install the four pivot bearings to Yamaha depths
steps.instruction: Pack new bearings and lubricate pivot stack with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Use fitting needle-support mandrel per Motion Pro figures3-4 and support housing squarely. OEM requires OUTER bearings first, then inner bearings at dimension b6.5mm measured from inside as shown. Record both sides. Do not substitute tool-example bottoming endpoint.
verification: Outer-before-inner order and both6.5mm positions recorded; fitted needles supported.

source_links.title: Motion Pro tool technique; Yamaha depths control

steps.title: Complete pivot bushes, thrust bearings and seals
steps.instruction: Restore two new matched bushes, two thrust bearings, four new seals and inspected collars in exact exploded order. Apply molybdenum grease. Measure all four seal recesses a0–0.5mm at illustrated bore faces; follow cross-section lip orientation and general marked-face-out guidance. Record each depth and stack.
verification: Four0–0.5mm seal readings and all side stacks recorded.

steps.title: Renew both relay-arm bearing pairs
steps.instruction: Install four relay bearings with fitting mandrels/supported housing at exact0mm bearing end-face locations. Molybdenum-grease bearings, washers, seals and collars. Restore inner washers, four new seals, matched collars and outer washers in exact exploded/cross-section order. Record flushness and both four-washer groups; bearing0mm is not a generic seal depth.
verification: Four relay bearings flush; eight washers in two correct groups; four seals and collars restored.

steps.title: Renew connecting-arm bearings
steps.instruction: Install two connecting-arm bearings at exact0mm illustrated bearing positions with fitting mandrels. Molybdenum-grease marked bearing/seal/collar surfaces. Restore two new seals and matched collar in shown orientation. Record bearing positions and smooth collar movement.
verification: Both bearing0mm positions recorded; no seal-depth inference.

steps.title: Record and expose the two mount stacks
steps.instruction: Photograph Yamaha PDF173/174 upper and lower stack orientations. Remove each pair of collars and dust seals; remove the upper O-rings. Identify the upper stopper ring and remove it before pressing the upper bushing. Lower eye has its separate bushing and bearing. Keep each eye supported locally and all spring/pressure components untouched.
verification: Upper/lower stacks identified separately
Upper stopper removed before bushing extraction
Spring, rod and pressure body not loaded

steps.title: Remove worn eye bearing components
steps.instruction: Use fitting mandrels and a centered receiver as in Motion Pro08-0294 figures1-2/5 to remove the upper bushing and lower bearing/bushing without stressing the shock rod or body. Verify the extraction path is unobstructed. Clean the empty seats and inspect for damage. A damaged mounting eye needs assembly repair/replacement beyond this operation; do not enlarge or stake the seat.
verification: Fitting local support recorded
No bore damage, retained fragments or obstructions

source_links.title: Motion Pro supported bearing tool technique only

steps.title: Install and retain upper bushing
steps.instruction: Press the upper bushing squarely by its outer race until its stopper-ring groove is exposed, as Yamaha PDF177 specifies. Install a new correct stopper ring fully in the groove. Push the bushing back until it contacts the ring. Lubricate the two new O-rings with lithium-soap grease and the upper dust-seal lips with molybdenum-disulfide grease at the PDF174 M arrows. Restore the upper seals and collars in PDF174 order and orientation.
verification: Stopper seated fully
Bushing returned into contact with stopper
Two new O-rings and two new seals correctly installed

steps.title: Renew lower bearing and seal stack
steps.instruction: Fit new lower bearing/bushing and correct collars to exact cross-section. Apply molybdenum grease to bearing and dust-seal lips but keep press-fit bearing outer race DRY as OEM warns. Fit two new dust seals lips inward. Measure each installed-depth a from the eye housing outer face to the bearing1 face shown in the exact cross-section:4.25mm. Do not substitute a seal or collar reference surface. Record both readings and smooth collar movement.
verification: Exact illustrated4.25mm a dimensions recorded both sides; dry outer race/M lips and inward seal lips confirmed.

steps.title: Install both new head races
steps.instruction: Use Motion Pro08-0669 page1 photographs for assembly. Clean the seats; test each new race on its driver. Fit tapered plate, washer and greased threaded rod with all nut threads engaged. Position the correctly oriented race/driver, pass the rod through, engage the locking plate and hand-snug. Draw in with24mm wrench, holding rod with14mm if needed. Watch alignment throughout; stop at the fully seated shoulder when resistance increases. Release and remove the tool; repeat for the other race. Unexpected resistance before seating requires inspection, not extra force.
verification: Both race orientations match Yamaha diagram
Both races aligned and fully seated; tool fit and observed seat condition recorded

steps.title: Install the lower seal and bearing
steps.instruction: Follow Motion Pro08-0544 page1 installation photographs. Clean stem and bracket seat. Restore the correct new dust seal before the bearing. Apply Yamaha lithium-soap grease to seal lip and bearing inner circumference. Select driver contacting only the inner race, clear of cage; use the HF adapter if required. Support the bracket underside on a protective block. Remove the tool puller bolt and use a soft mallet to seat the new bearing. Inspect full seating and intact seal/cage; grease the bearing.
verification: Correct seal stack installed before bearing
Driver loaded inner race only
Full bearing seating and undamaged seal/cage recorded

steps.title: Restore footrests, roller and retained mounting pieces
steps.instruction: Return all labeled rubber pieces and clip-in holders to their original positions. Refit the intact footrest brackets with source-specified LOCTITE on the four bolts and tighten55 N·m. Refit the intact lower chain-tensioner roller and collar stack and tighten its bolt16 N·m; check the roller turns correctly.
verification: Footrest bolts55 N·m; lower roller16 N·m and free; original mount pieces restored.

steps.title: Reinstall the rear frame and upper roller
steps.instruction: Align the supported rear frame without trapping wires. Return all four mounting bolts to their mapped positions and tighten to 38 Nm. Refit the separately mounted upper chain roller with its original collar stack and tighten its bolt to 16 Nm. Confirm it turns freely.
verification: Four rear-frame bolts 38 Nm; separate upper roller bolt 16 Nm; roller turns freely.

steps.title: Place the controls, loom and brackets back on the frame
steps.instruction: Restore supported throttle-body/cable and bar/closed-brake assemblies near original positions. Route loom along exact tank-rail path and engage frame projections. Refit regulator7Nm and frame ground7Nm at original locations. ECU and coil stay on removed aircase until that closure. Injector/pressure/TPS remain disconnected until engine/body refit. Preserve connector covers and supports without trapping harness in engine opening.
verification: Regulator/frame ground7Nm; frame locators seated; retained groups supported and engine opening clear.

steps.title: Restore rear harness routing and holders
steps.instruction: Restore main relay, starter relay and CCU couplers/covers and battery bracket clips. Route starter/relay tie within20mm cross-tube width, lock DOWN, tail INSIDE rear frame UNCUT. Starter lead follows inside rear frame/rear fender; restore exact pink fuel-hose and white harness tape markers, original slack and remaining trim exceptions per right-side drawing. Both battery leads go UNDER crossmember; their relative order is unrestricted. Fit battery/band but leave terminals isolated.
verification: Exact2022 rear tie directions/uncut exception and lead paths restored; battery remains isolated.

steps.title: Mount the radiators and route their hoses
steps.instruction: Inspect hoses and mounting dampers for damage. Restore the original damper/collar/washer stacks and tighten the four radiator mounting bolts10 N·m. Return hoses1–4 to their labeled radiator ends, preserving the original clamp positions; disturbed hose-clamp screws tighten1.5 N·m. Leave engine-end joints ready for engine installation. Route radiator breather behind the upper boss, behind the cylinder-head breather, ahead of the lower boss and ahead of the radiator hose, then through the down tube as shown.
verification: Radiator mounts10 N·m; radiator-side clamps1.5 N·m; breather and hoses correctly routed.

steps.title: Hang the intact shock on its upper mount
steps.instruction: Verify the completed new upper bushing/stopper/seals and correctly seated collars and lubricate the upper mounting bolt with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Install the bolt from the right and tighten its nut56 N·m. Keep the sealed shock supported until its lower connection is restored; no preload or internal changes are implied.
verification: Upper bolt from right; nut56 N·m; new bushing/stopper/O-rings/seals and correct collars verified.

steps.title: Lubricate the bearing stack
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the bearings, dust-seal/race-cover lips, steering-stem threads and the stem portion shown in the OEM illustration. Return the lower bracket with its newly fitted lower bearing, install the NEW matching upper bearing and race cover in the illustrated order. Fit the ring nut with its stepped side downward.
verification: Lubricated bearing/cover stack correct; ring-nut step faces down.

steps.title: Set the steering preload
steps.instruction: Hold the torque wrench at a right angle to the steering-nut wrench. Tighten the ring nut initially to 38 N·m and turn the steering left/right several times. If it binds, inspect the bearings. Loosen the ring nut one full turn, then retighten to 7 N·m. Check full lock-to-lock movement without play or binding.
verification: Initial 38 N·m, loosen one turn, final 7 N·m; smooth steering without looseness.

steps.title: Restore the upper bracket and stem nut
steps.instruction: Install the washer and upper bracket. Slide the fork legs into place and temporarily secure the lower clamps, leaving the upper pinch bolts loose. Grease the steering-stem nut contact surface with lithium-soap grease and tighten the stem nut to 145 N·m. Check steering again; if movement is not smooth, follow the manual ring-nut adjustment rather than proceeding.
verification: Washer fitted; stem nut 145 N·m; steering smooth.

steps.title: Refit and secure the top assemblies
steps.instruction: With the legs temporarily held by the lower clamps and the upper pinch bolts still loose, tighten each damper assembly at the top to 30 N·m using the cap ring wrench. Keep each leg supported.
verification: Legs supported; top damper assemblies 30 N·m; upper clamps still loose.

steps.title: Set height and tighten the clamps
steps.instruction: With each leg supported, set its outer-tube top projection to 5 mm using the exact source-diagram reference. Match both sides. Tighten upper and lower clamp pinch bolts to 21 N·m; do not overtorque the lower clamps.
verification: Both actual5mm projections recorded; both clamps21Nm.

steps.title: Restore the handlebar and fender
steps.instruction: Refit front fender with four bolts10Nm. Restore four dampers and original washer/holder stack; lower-holder longer-offset side faces rear in the standard orientation, or restore recorded source-permitted reversed offset if previously confirmed. Refit the complete bar/holder assembly in its recorded positions and tighten both lower-holder nuts40Nm. Upper holders/bar alignment remained clamped; do not repeat their undisturbed bolt operation. Confirm secure bar, clear controls and full steering movement; verify no tank contact after tank refit.
verification: Fender10Nm; four dampers and original offset correct; both lower-holder nuts40Nm; upper-holder bolts retained.

steps.title: Lubricate the sliding and cable-end surfaces
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the throttle-grip sliding surface. Lightly grease the cable ends and inside of the grip as shown. Keep grease away from the exterior gripping surface and the brake.
verification: Sliding and cable-end contact surfaces lubricated.

steps.title: Reconnect pull and return cables
steps.instruction: Restore each identified cable end to its original seat and groove in the throttle tube. Place the rubber cover and slide the intact grip/tube onto the handlebar. Confirm both cable ends and their outer housings are seated correctly before closing the housing.
verification: Both cable ends seated in the correct positions without crossing.

steps.title: Secure the housing
steps.instruction: Fit the housing and tighten its screws to 3.8 Nm. Check grip movement immediately. If the housing causes binding, reposition and retighten it, then check again. Restore the housing cover and rubber cover.
verification: Housing torqued; grip moves smoothly and returns.

steps.title: Restore protectors and brake mounts
steps.instruction: Refit the protectors at 5 N·m per bolt. Refit the complete caliper to the fork and tighten its two mount bolts to 28 N·m. Align the upper end of the hose holder with the hose paint mark and tighten its bolts to 9 N·m, preserving the original routing.
verification: Protectors5Nm, caliper28Nm and original hose holder9Nm with source paint-mark alignment.

steps.title: Install the wheel and axle
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap grease to the axle and wheel oil-seal lips. Put the side-specific collars back, lift the wheel into place with the disc correctly between the pads, and insert the axle. Thread the axle nut on by hand; leave its final tightening and the axle pinch bolts for the seating step.
verification: Collars correct; disc between pads; axle inserted; nut retained; final torques pending.

steps.title: Restore front control routing
steps.instruction: Route clutch cable behind number-plate band and through plate guide. Brake hose passes FRONT of number plate. Start/launch leads pass LEFT of plate bracket. Engine-stop/mode and start leads pass between frame and cable guide. Restore handlebar lead ties as shown, ends UNCUT. Do not inherit newer-year plate upper/lower brake-hose guides.
verification: Exact2022 clutch, brake and switch lead paths; uncut tie ends restored.

steps.title: Verify free play and return before starting
steps.instruction: With the engine stopped, check free play and smooth full return through the steering travel. The retained setup must still have 3–6 mm free play and no binding. If not, correct seating/routing before starting; do not use a running engine to diagnose a bound throttle.
verification: Record 3–6 mm free play and full return at centre and both steering limits.

steps.title: Restore guides and settings
steps.instruction: Engage plate on LOWER STEERING BRACKET projection, place clutch cable in its guide and secure plate projection in band UPPER hole. Keep brake hose in front. Plate bolt7Nm. Restore recorded fork rebound/compression via gently seated hard reference, matching intended sides.
verification: Plate lower-bracket/band/clutch routing correct7Nm; original clickers restored.

steps.title: Verify the engine and rear bearing stacks
steps.instruction: Confirm documented checks for any separate internal work; engine internals remain assembled here. Verify renewed swingarm side stacks and all measured depths. Molybdenum-grease specified contacts and position supported swingarm with renewed stacks. Next shared pivot locates both arm and engine once.
verification: Renewed swingarm stacks/depths and any separate internal record accepted; single pivot replacement ready.

steps.title: Place the engine back in the chassis
steps.instruction: Bring supported engine in from the right, lower part first. Align mounts without trapping hoses or leads. Apply molybdenum-disulfide grease to the pivot shaft and insert from the right while withdrawing temporary support, preserving newly renewed swingarm side stacks. No lithium grease on pivot-nut threads is specified here.
verification: Engine and swingarm aligned; M-greased pivot from right; no newer-year nut preparation inherited.

steps.title: Install and secure the engine brackets
steps.instruction: Restore two lower brackets and four shims with shim projections toward the outside of the bike, plus both upper brackets and mapped hardware. Follow installation sequence: pivot nut85Nm; lower mount53Nm; front bracket bolts34Nm; front engine mount55Nm; upper bracket bolts34Nm; upper mounts45Nm. Keep the assembly supported/aligned throughout.
verification: Shim projections outward; recorded85/53/34/55/34/45Nm at exact labeled joints.

steps.title: Refit the linkage in its original orientation
steps.instruction: Lubricate only connecting-arm-to-relay and relay-to-swingarm bolt circumference/threads with molybdenum grease. Fit both from LEFT with renewed collars/seals and correct washers. Keep frame-side connecting-arm and lower-shock joints supported but OPEN for exhaust refit clearance. Their two bolts close in the explicit post-exhaust step.
verification: Two internal linkage bolts from LEFT; frame/lower-shock clearance joints remain supported/open.

steps.title: Secure the linkage and lower shock
steps.instruction: Tighten connecting-arm-to-relay nut80Nm and relay-to-swingarm nut70Nm. Upper shock already restored56Nm. Keep frame connecting-arm and lower shock bolts out until exhaust closure; do not load unsupported suspension.
verification: Relay80/70Nm; upper56Nm recorded; other two joints deliberately deferred.

steps.title: Mount the closed rear brake assembly
steps.instruction: Refit the rear master cylinder with both mounting bolts at 10 Nm, retaining its pushrod/clevis adjustment. Restore the hose to all swingarm holders with the exact illustrated route, no excessive twist and no interference with the spring. Verify the undisturbed hose metal ends remain against their master/caliper stops. Keep the caliper/bracket supported for wheel insertion; the engine closure step restores pedal pivot and spring. Restore any removed hose-holder mounting screws to 3.5 Nm.
verification: Master mount bolts10 N·m; closed hose correctly routed; pedal/clevis unchanged.

steps.title: Reconnect and adjust the cable clutch
steps.instruction: Restore the identified clutch cable outer to its engine bracket and nipple to the push lever as illustrated; tighten the engine-end cable locknut to 7 Nm if loosened. Verify full seating. Set lever free play to 7-12 mm using the handlebar adjuster first. If its range is insufficient, slide the cable cover, loosen the cable-side adjuster locknut, adjust and tighten that locknut to 4.3 Nm, then restore the cover. Check smooth clutch operation through both steering locks and record actual free play.
verification: Engine cable-end and outer fully seated; disturbed engine locknut 7 Nm; cable-side adjuster locknut 4.3 Nm if used; actual lever free play 7-12 mm recorded.

steps.title: Restore pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Install new pedal-pivot O-rings in both illustrated positions with lithium-soap grease. Grease pivot/seal contacts as shown and restore pivot bolt26Nm and return spring; engine guard7Nm. Restore head breather at engine and original holders: between radiator hose and engine bracket, outlet down aligned with lower down tube. Keep it clear of lower/front engine bosses and route radiator breather around it as illustrated.
verification: Two new LS pedal seals;26/7Nm; head breather points down in exact route, not into aircase.

steps.title: Restore the drive sprocket and chain
steps.instruction: Fit the original serviceable drive sprocket and new correct lock washer. Leave the nut hand-threaded temporarily; its final torque and tab locking are a later explicit step after rear-wheel, brake and chain closure. Align shift-shaft/pedal punch marks and tighten the pedal bolt to 12 Nm. Fit the retained stock chain with matched link/plate and new clip, closed end leading chain travel as illustrated; lubricate the chain. Leave the sprocket cover off for the final nut check.
verification: Original sprocket and new lock washer seated; nut temporary only; new chain clip correctly oriented; shift pedal 12 Nm.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and chain
steps.instruction: Grease the oil-seal lips with lithium-soap-based grease and refit the collars. Place the disc between the brake pads and locate the caliper bracket correctly in its swingarm guide. Keep the chain removed for now; the later explicit sprocket/chain step installs and joins it. Fit the left puller and insert the greased axle from the left.
verification: Wheel/disc/caliper bracket and left greased axle located; chain remains removed until its explicit installation step.

steps.title: Fit the right puller and nut
steps.instruction: Fit the right chain puller, washer and axle nut. Leave the nut temporarily snug until chain adjustment is complete.
verification: Right puller and washer present; axle nut temporary only.

steps.title: Restore the engine ground and starter lead
steps.instruction: Restore head ground terminal at its illustrated location7Nm; exact routing permits its terminal to face either way, so retain original untensioned routing. Restore starter lead6Nm while holding motor-side nut and replace rubber terminal cover. Restore its clamps and lead path along cylinder without slack.
verification: Ground7Nm/starter6Nm; terminal supported during tightening; rubber cover/lead route restored.

steps.title: Reconnect and route the engine harness
steps.instruction: Reconnect labeled stator, crank-position, gear-position and coolant-temperature couplers/covers. Stator passes behind radiator without tension-arm pinch; gear lead follows case inside front engine bracket without slack. Clutch cable must not sag down; protector contacts radiator hose outside stator/gear leads. Regulator leads stay inside tension arm. Restore frame clip lock forward and trim where shown; starter lead follows cylinder without slack. Reproduce the exact left/right routing and tie positions, distinguishing trimmed ties from those the source says leave uncut.
verification: All identified engine couplers latched; cable/lead separation and exact ties restored; no inherited newer-year grommet arrangement.

steps.title: Reseat the throttle body
steps.instruction: Remove intake protection and seat the intact throttle body fully in its original engine-side joint. Restore the clamp orientation and tighten the throttle-body joint clamp to 3.0 N·m. Keep both cables routed without tension and check full smooth throttle return. Sensors and calibration screws remain untouched. Reconnect all three labeled injector/pressure/TPS couplers without moving sensors.
verification: Joint fully seated 3.0 N·m; throttle returns smoothly; cables not trapped.

steps.title: Reconnect the engine coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Remove temporary port covers. Restore radiator hoses 1,3 and 4 to their marked engine connections and original clamp positions; tighten each disturbed radiator-hose clamp screw to 1.5 N·m. Check there are no kinks or trapped hoses. Radiator pipe seals and temperature sensor were not removed.
verification: Hoses 1/3/4 correct; disturbed clamps 1.5 N·m.

steps.title: Seat the new header gasket
steps.instruction: Install the new exhaust-port gasket at the cylinder head and refit header pipe 1. Tighten all header nuts first to 7 N·m, then retighten them to 10 N·m. Do not apply the protector-screw locking-agent note to these nuts.
verification: New exhaust-port gasket; all header nuts 7 then 10 Nm.

steps.title: Locate pipe 2 and its clamp
steps.instruction: Install new joint gaskets in the exact exploded locations. Refit clamp, pipe2 and bracket bolt. Engage clamp projection in pipe/silencer slot and keep clamp off the raised pipe projection. Leave final clamp/bracket torque until silencer is seated.
verification: New joint seals and clamp projection/slot alignment correct.

steps.title: Refit the complete silencer
steps.instruction: Refit the silencer clamp and complete silencer on the seated joint. Install the retained mounting hardware and tighten both silencer mounting bolts to 30 N·m.
verification: Both silencer mounts 30 N·m; joints fully engaged.

steps.title: Tighten the bracket and both clamps
steps.instruction: Confirm front and rear joints remain fully inserted while tightening the exhaust-pipe bracket bolt to 20 N·m, pipe-2 clamp bolt to 12 N·m and silencer clamp bolt to 12 N·m.
verification: Bracket 20 N·m; each joint clamp 12 N·m; projections correctly located.

steps.title: Restore the two suspension access joints
steps.instruction: With exhaust fully seated and torqued, align supported shock lower and connecting-arm frame joints with their newly renewed collars/seals. Apply molybdenum-disulfide grease to the disturbed bolt circumference and threads. Insert connecting-arm frame bolt from RIGHT and shock lower bolt from LEFT. Tighten frame connecting-arm nut80Nm and shock lower nut53Nm. Inspect unobstructed movement and full seating; retain support until closure is verified.
verification: Correct bolt directions, M grease, frame80Nm and shock lower53Nm; no trapped seal or binding.

steps.title: Seat the case and secure its mounts
steps.instruction: Remove intake protection and seat complete aircase with retained ECU, coil and filter onto its original joint. Restore collars, dampers and washers; three case bolts7Nm and joint clamp3Nm. Reconnect labeled ECU, coil and intake-temperature couplers/covers. Restore sub-lead between ECU and case and clips fully against ribs; keep harness clear of rails/intake joint. Fully seat plug cap facing right within the illustrated10-degree range. ECU/coil mounts remain untouched.
verification: Three7Nm case bolts/3Nm clamp; case-mounted electronics connected and original orientation preserved; plug cap fully seated facing right.

steps.title: Verify the restored intake
steps.instruction: Check case support, fully seated intake joints, reconnects and retained ECU/coil mounts. Verify no temporary covers remain and no wire lies pinched under case or between frame rail and joint. Filter remains correctly seated.
verification: Sealed supported intake and retained electronics; all protection removed.

steps.title: Reconnect the fuel system
steps.instruction: Restore tank on its original four dampers and retained collars. Tighten two front mounts7Nm and rear retaining screw9Nm. Remove joint covers, press fuel joint until click and lock cover/holder. Reconnect white2-pin pump connector. Route BOTH fuel hose and pump lead through cover guide; keep pump lead outside hose, hose ahead of battery, with no pinch/kink.
verification: Tank7/9Nm at exact mounts; fuel joint clicked/locked; both hose and lead guided.

steps.title: Refill with the specified mixture
steps.instruction: Use the specified aluminum-compatible ethylene-glycol antifreeze and distilled water at a final 1:1 coolant-to-water ratio. Do not mix antifreeze types. Fill to the maximum level illustrated in PDF96. The complete system nominal volume is 1.03 L including all routes; correct level and concentration govern, not forcing in that amount after an incomplete drain. Wash any spill on paint away immediately with water.
verification: Mixture/product and amount recorded; level at illustrated maximum.

steps.title: Secure the radiator cap
steps.instruction: Install and secure the radiator cap. Account for the drain hardware, collection container and tools before running the engine.
verification: Cap secured; drain sealed; tools clear.

steps.title: Pressure-check the reinstalled cooling system
steps.instruction: With coolant at the upper level, install the specified radiator tester/adapter and apply137.3 kPa; do not exceed that pressure. It must hold5–10 seconds. Check radiator joints and hoses for leaks or bulging, correct any fault, release pressure and cover the connection with a cloth before removing the tester. Secure the radiator cap. Do not perform this check on a hot pressurized system.
verification: Cooling system holds137.3 kPa for5–10 seconds; no leaks/bulges; cap restored.

steps.title: Refill the oil for the actual engine condition
steps.instruction: Record applicable oil quantity:.63L unchanged filter,.65L filter removal,.90L disassembled engine. Use source-listed Yamalube/API SG-or-higher JASO MA with SAE10W40,10W50,15W40,20W40 or20W50 selected against the ambient-temperature chart. No additives. Record product and actual quantity, check filler cap/seal condition and install cap. Do not copy newer-year filler O-ring grease/replacement instructions absent here. Flow and exact final level checks remain required.
verification: Actual oil product and case-specific quantity recorded; cap secure; no unsupported filler torque/preparation.

steps.title: Reconnect the battery and inspect routing
steps.instruction: Recheck interfaces, reconnect positive before negative and restore positive cover. Both battery leads pass UNDER the crossmember; source permits either relative order. Negative lead coupler sits right of starter relay; restore battery bracket clips and protect all conductors from frame contact.
verification: Positive then negative; both under crossmember; covers/clips restored.

steps.title: Refit the panels and seat
steps.instruction: Fit air-scoop projections into aircase holes, grooves over ribs and remaining projections into slots; bolts7Nm. Refit aircase cover with its two rear slots engaging case edges and left/right ribs aligned with scoop projections; secure quick-fastener screw and restore fuel breather to cover as illustrated. Refit right-cover projections/slots with its rib under rear-fender rib. Slide seat forward and secure its two bolts22Nm; ordinary cover fasteners7Nm. Restore fuel-cap cover with attached plastic bands all the way under seat.
verification: Scoop/cover locators seated;22Nm seat and7Nm ordinary covers; cap-cover bands under seat; breather restored.

steps.title: Measure and adjust chain slack
steps.instruction: Loosen the rear axle nut and both adjuster locknuts first. With the rear wheel raised and gearbox in neutral, pull the chain upward above the chain-guide mounting bolt with about 50 N. Measure between the drive-chain guide and the bottom of the chain at the exact diagram location. Adjust both sides equally to 50–60 mm. Push the wheel forward so each puller/end plate is seated against the swingarm end.
verification: Measured slack 50–60 mm using OEM50 N reference; pullers equally adjusted and seated.

steps.title: Secure the rear axle and adjusters
steps.instruction: Tighten the rear axle nut to 135 N·m and both chain-adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m. Recheck the chain slack after tightening.
verification: Axle 135 N·m; locknuts 21 N·m; final slack recorded.

steps.title: Lock the drive sprocket after rear-wheel closure
steps.instruction: With rear axle and adjusters torqued, chain installed and rear brake firm, keep neutral and have a helper hold the rear brake. Tighten the hand-fitted sprocket nut90Nm with a torque wrench. The exact2022 source gives no locking-agent preparation for this nut; do not inherit it from another year. Bend the new lock-washer tabs firmly against the nut flats. Restore the retained chain guide/bracket and cover at7Nm. No impact, heat or case jamming.

source_links.title: Nick Dole manual rear-brake holding technique

verification: Nut90Nm/new washer tabs locked; original guide/bracket restored; cover7Nm; brake holding load controlled.

steps.title: Check chain alignment and brake function
steps.instruction: With wheel on final-torqued axle and supported off ground, verify rotation, bearing play and brake function. Measure radial/lateral runout using stable dial gauge at exact rim locations; each limit2mm. Save replacements, spacer/circlip checks and documented seal-endpoint plus actual positions. Resolve binding or out-of-limit runout before use.
verification: Runout both2mm-or-less; bearings smooth; documented seal endpoints/actual positions retained.

steps.title: Seat the forks before final axle tightening
steps.instruction: With the bike securely supported on its wheels, push down on the handlebars several times and confirm smooth fork rebound before final axle-nut tightening, as Yamaha specifies. Tighten the axle nut to 115 N·m, then all four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m. This is a stationary seating operation, not permission to ride with loose axle hardware.
verification: Smooth rebound before nut torque; axle nut 115 N·m; four axle pinch bolts 21 N·m.

steps.title: Verify steering and front-end closure
steps.instruction: After final axle tightening, check steering free from play/binding, smooth fork action, firm front brake and clear hoses. With front wheel raised on its torqued axle verify rotation/play and record radial/lateral runout at exact rim locations using stable gauge; each limit2mm. Resolve any binding or out-of-limit wheel.
verification: Steering/fork/brake/wheel checks complete; both runout readings2mm-or-less.

steps.title: Restore fuel and verify readiness to start
steps.instruction: Lift fuel-cap cover and add clean recommended unleaded minimum91(R+M)/2 gasoline; E10 permitted. Secure cap and restore cover with bands under seat. Verify latched pump connector and fuel hose/holder and no fuel leak. Select neutral in a ventilated area before starter operation.
verification: Correct fuel/cap/cover; no leaks; neutral and ventilation.

steps.title: Verify oil flow immediately at idle
steps.instruction: Start only after fuel, intake, cooling, electrical and mounting closure is complete. Keep the engine at idle; observe the oil-check window for oil flow and decreasing level. If the level does not decrease, stop the engine immediately and investigate the lubrication system instead of revving it.
verification: Oil flow/level decrease observed at idle; no leak or abnormal condition.

steps.title: Warm for the operating checks
steps.instruction: After initial idle oil-flow verification and with all fuel, cooling, intake and control closure complete, warm the engine for several minutes. Leave the radiator cap secured. Proceed to the following measured operating checks before stopping and cooling completely.
verification: Initial oil flow verified; engine warmed for the next measured operating checks; cap remains closed.

steps.title: Check the warm idle
steps.instruction: Use the correctly configured YDT 90890-03269 (US USB) or 90890-03264 to confirm coolant at 70–80 °C. Measure speed with tachometer 90890-06760 or YU-39951-B, connected as shown to the ignition-coil high-tension lead. With the starter knob fully returned and normal filter/compression/free play, verify 1900–2100 r/min. If necessary, adjust the idle screw; clockwise raises speed.
verification: Record temperature and accepted idle speed.

steps.title: Set the final grip free play
steps.instruction: Stop the engine. If final adjustment is needed after idle setting, loosen the grip adjuster locknut, turn the adjuster to obtain 3–6 mm free play, and tighten the locknut. Confirm smooth full return again.
verification: Record final 3–6 mm free play and secure locknut.

steps.title: Verify idle through steering travel
steps.instruction: Restart the warm engine without starter enrichment. Turn the handlebar fully left and right: idle must not change. If it changes, stop and correct cable routing/seating or adjustment before repeating this check. Hold the engine-stop switch until the engine fully stops when the check is finished.
verification: Record unchanged idle across steering travel; engine stopped.

steps.title: Allow complete cooling
steps.instruction: After the operating check has stopped the engine, let it cool completely before opening the radiator cap for the next cold-level check.
verification: Engine stopped and fully cooled before the cap is opened.

steps.title: Recheck the cold level
steps.instruction: Keep the bike upright on level ground. With the engine cooled, use the cloth and slow pressure-release method to remove the cap. Allow the coolant to settle, check against the illustrated maximum and add the correct mixture if low. Restore the cap securely. A leak or repeatedly dropping level requires repair rather than repeated top-offs.
verification: Final cold level and mixture recorded; cap secured; no unresolved loss.

steps.title: Verify the installed engine and record closure
steps.instruction: Follow exact oil-level method upright on level ground: warm2-3minutes, stop and wait about1minute. Verify oil above the minimum window mark. Place a container, remove the identified level-check bolt and verify oil does not run out; if it does, drain excess until last drop. If at/below minimum, add correct oil above minimum and repeat exact check. Restore check bolt/seal using the documented exact-interface closure obtained before work; record source, actual torque and seal action. Do not restart or return to use with this closure unresolved. Check leaks, clutch7-12mm, throttle3-6mm/full return, brakes firm, chain50-60mm and recorded warm steering idle. Record mount/fluid/support closure and any separate bench record.
verification: Actual final level and documented check-bolt closure recorded; all fluid/chain/control/support checks complete; no unresolved leak/binding.

steps.title: Verify the rebuilt chassis as a whole
steps.instruction: Verify steering/lock clearance, smooth suspension, both wheel/brake functions, chain, footrest return, all disturbed fasteners and fluids. Record separate engine/component work and faults. With tank installed verify bar does not contact tank at either lock. Confirm wheel seal positions against documented exact endpoints, wheel bearing/spacer/circlip stacks, steering seats, swingarm6.5mm and0–0.5mm seals, linkage0mm bearings and shock-eye4.25mm reference. Exact oil-check-bolt closure must be recorded. No housing refit implies unperformed renewal; no structural repair or physical validation is claimed.
verification: All real measurement/closure records saved; external oilbolt/wheel endpoints accounted; no unresolved defect concealed.
